title: Bhrigu and the layers of a person
hookLine: a son asks his father what is ultimately real, and finds a person has layers
carry: the subtle body: more of you than flesh
tomorrow: the old map starts with someone asleep at the bottom. who?

cards: In the Taittiriya Upanishad, a young man named Bhrigu goes to his father, the god Varuna, and asks: teach me Brahman, the ultimate reality. Varuna doesn't lecture. He points: food, breath, sight, hearing, mind, speech.
Then he says: that from which beings are born, by which they live, into which they return, seek that. Seek it through tapas, steady disciplined effort. Go and practice.
Bhrigu goes off, works at it, and comes back sure. It's food; everything is made of it. Go again, says his father.

teach.b: So he goes again. Breath, he decides next, the life that moves the body. Go again.
Then mind. Then understanding. And at last, joy, ananda, and this time he isn't sent back.
The same Upanishad describes a person in five koshas, sheaths, each finer than the last: the body made of food, then breath, mind, understanding and bliss.

Vedanta groups the middle three into the sukshma sharira, the subtle body: a real part of you that isn't made of flesh. That's the big teaching: you are more than the body you can weigh. And it's where the chakras live.
Chakra means a wheel or a circle, and the yoga texts place them in the subtle body, along the spine, pictured as lotuses. Now the modern argument: no scan has ever found one.
Inside the tradition there are two answers, and each deserves its best case. One view: of course not.
A scanner sees the body made of food, Bhrigu's first answer, and the subtle body was never said to be tissue.

teach.h: CHAKRAS: WHEELS IN THE SUBTLE BODY.
teach.b: Another view, held by many teachers: the chakras are a map for meditation, telling you where to rest attention, and a map is tested by walking it.

teach.h: NO SCAN FINDS THEM: TWO ANSWERS.

teach.b: Neither calls the chakras organs. Bhrigu's first answer wasn't wrong. It was only the first layer.

how: Hindu teaching describes a person in five sheaths (koshas), and Vedanta speaks of a gross, a subtle and a causal body; the chakras are placed in the subtle body and taught inside meditation, usually with a teacher. Some teachers stress the subtle body as real, others the chakras as a sequence for placing attention.

games.q: what does “the chakras as a map” mean?
o: centers on the body, read as a guide for attention
hidden organs that a good scan could someday find
colored lights that switch on during a hard workout

games.q: a person in layers — tap the pairs.
p: asked his father to teach him Brahman
a sheath, one layer of a person
the subtle body, not made of flesh
sees the body made of food

s: Bhrigu's first answer, food, was the end of his search
his father sent him back again and again: breath, mind, understanding, joy.
chakra is the Sanskrit word for a wheel or a circle
the texts use it for centers along the spine, pictured as lotuses.
if a scan can't find chakras, the tradition has been proven wrong
the tradition places them in the subtle body, which was never said to be tissue.

games.q: you lean toward the map view. a friend calls the subtle-body view plain superstition. what's that view's best case, in its own terms?
o: it never claimed tissue; like Bhrigu's layers, it describes a person finer than the body a scan sees.
machines will catch up one day and photograph the chakras.
the chakras are really nerves the old writers named differently.
games.why: that's the view as its holders put it. the other two answers turn it into a claim about tissue, which is the one thing it doesn't say.

practice: Close your eyes and climb Bhrigu's layers. Feel the body's weight on the seat. Then the breath moving.
Then thoughts passing. Then notice the one who's noticing all of it, and rest there. If you pray, you can offer that stillness; if not, simply stay with it.

wordCard.voice: The chakras as a map: centers along the spine, pictured as lotuses, placed by the tradition in the subtle body, not in tissue.

orig.note: Sanskrit: a wheel or circle; in the yoga texts, a center along the spine.

carryVoice: Your line: the subtle body, more of you than flesh. Bhrigu kept going past the first layer. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Taittiriya Upanishad 3 (Bhrigu asks Varuna to teach him Brahman; sent back to practice, he realizes food, breath, mind, understanding and bliss in turn)
Taittiriya Upanishad 2 (the person in five sheaths: food, breath, mind, understanding, bliss)
the subtle body (sukshma sharira) in Vedanta teaching, comprising the sheaths of breath, mind and understanding
Sat-Cakra-Nirupana (the cakras as centers along the spine, pictured as lotuses for meditation)
